passages.original: Quando, rogo, volunt illam synodum coram Theodosio Mediolani congre- gatam? Num cum primum, adversus Maximum tyrannum pugnaturus, Constantinopoli anna decimo sui im- perii in Italiam venit? Certe id dici non posse, quae sanctus Hieronymus scribit, vehementer repugnant : dum enim in libro de Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis, ad calcem, cunctas quas hactenus usque ad annum decimum quartum eiusdem Theodosii imperatoris elaborasset lucubrationes, recenset, nec verbum quidem de con- scripto, vela se translato libro de Martyribus habet, quem statim post illam synodum scriptum esse, illae ipsae recitatae epistolae indicant : ex quibus satis apparet, dictam synodum commentitiam ad primum Theo- dosii Mediolanum adventum non posse referri.
passages.english: When, I ask, do they claim that synod was assembled at Milan in the presence of Theodosius? Was it when he first came from Constantinople into Italy in the tenth year of his reign, to fight against the usurper Maximus? Certainly, what Saint Jerome writes strongly contradicts the claim that this can be said. For in the book On Ecclesiastical Writers, at the end, where he lists all the works he had produced up to the fourteenth year of that same emperor Theodosius, he has not even a word about a book On the Martyrs, whether written or translated by him; and the very letters that were quoted indicate that this book was written immediately after that synod. From this it is quite clear that the said fictitious synod cannot be assigned to Theodosius' first coming to Milan.
passages.notes: "anna" read as "anno"; "vela se" read as "vel a se".

passages.original: Constat, Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum omni die martyrum suorum triumphos excipere, quorum passiones a sancto Eusebio Caesariensi epis- copo scriptas reperimus. Nam Constantinus Augus- tus cum Caesaream fuisset ingresus, et diceret memorato antistiti, ut peteret aliqua beneficia Cae- sariensi Ecclesiae profutura, legitur, respondisse Eusebium : Opibus suis Ecclesiam ditatam, nulla petendi beneficia necessitate compelli : sibi tamen desiderium immobile exstitisse, ut quidquid in re- publica Romana gestum sit erga sanctos Dei judices judicibus succedentes in universo orbe Romano, sollicita perscrutatione, monumenta publica discu- tiendo, perquirerent;
passages.english: It is established that our Lord Jesus Christ every day receives the triumphs of his martyrs, whose passions we find were written by Saint Eusebius, bishop of Caesarea. For when Constantine Augustus had entered Caesarea and told the aforementioned bishop to ask for some benefits that would be of use to the Church of Caesarea, Eusebius is read to have replied that the Church, enriched by its own resources, was under no necessity to ask for benefits; but that he himself had an unchanging desire that whatever had been done in the Roman state against the saints of God, the judges succeeding [other] judges throughout the whole Roman world should search out with careful investigation by examining the public records;
passages.notes: "erga sanctos Dei" taken in the hostile sense "against"; "ingresus" read as "ingressus". The sentence continues in the following text.
